interpretation: 'When it combines in this way, affirming or denying, it is true; when in that way, false' (ὅταν μὲν ὡδὶ συνθῇ φᾶσα ἢ ἀποφᾶσα, ἀληθεύει, ὅταν δὲ ὡδί, ψεύδεται), read with the definition of truth at 1011b26-27 (to say of what is that it is, and of what is not that it is not, is true). An affirmation is true exactly when its object holds and false exactly when it does not; a denial the reverse. Taken as biconditionals because Aristotle gives a definition. This is a realist (correspondence) account: truth depends on how things are, not on whether the thought has been verified.
